components.text: OneNote: best if you want the most polished free Android + web sync experience, but its free storage cap is the main constraint.
Simplenote: best for plain text notes and lightweight syncing across Android and web.
Joplin: best for offline use and exportable, user-owned notes, with sync flexibility rather than a large free cloud quota.
Current source coverage is enough to compare core limits, but detailed free-tier export rules are not fully specified for every app.

comparison_data.offline: Works offline on Android and web-backed notebooks sync when you reconnect[2][12]
comparison_data.export: Export support is available, but the free plan is mainly limited by storage rather than format
comparison_data.restriction: About 5 GB of notes on the free plan

comparison_data.offline: Supports offline editing, with changes syncing later across devices[7]
comparison_data.sync: Syncs across Android and browser-based access
comparison_data.export: Exports are supported through account data export tools, though not highlighted as a major free-tier feature in the sources
comparison_data.restriction: No major paid wall is emphasized in the source; the practical limitation is its very minimal feature set

comparison_data.offline: Designed for offline-first use with local note storage[4][5]
comparison_data.sync: Sync is available, but setup depends on the sync method you choose
comparison_data.export: Strong portability: notes are stored locally and can be exported as files you control
comparison_data.restriction: The main free-plan limitation is that advanced sync convenience is not bundled as a paid-less, turnkey service
